rationale:
# rationale
The proposed topology employs a tapped inductor-loaded common-source amplifier with source degeneration, optimized for high gain and low noise at 2.44 GHz. The inductive degeneration (Lg) and tuned load (Ld, Ct1, Ct2) enable excellent input matching (S11) and high transconductance gain while maintaining a low noise figure. The tapped load structure (Ct1, Ct2) provides impedance transformation that enhances S21 and enables simultaneous input and output matching within the 45nm CMOS process constraints. The topology avoids floating nodes, respects the device budget, and uses only three inductors—within the allowed limit—while ensuring the input is driven through a grounded gate (no floating gate issues). The structure is robust to process and temperature variations due to its passive tuning and high Q inductors, and the absence of a cascode or resistive load preserves current efficiency and avoids unnecessary Idd overhead. The architecture is well-suited to meet the NF ≤ 2.5 dB, S11 ≤ -10 dB, S21 ≥ 12 dB, and Idd ≤ 5 mA targets.
